findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Observed that 12 cans were severely dented, top or bottom seams, or dents severe enough to cause sharp edges. CORRECTED: PICs were notified and cans were discarded. Inspector discussed protecting can integrity with PIC, including what type of damage should lead to cans being rejected. Ensure that canned packaging is in good condition so the food inside is protected from potential contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed there is an accumulation of food residue, grease, and other debris on the floor in the chemical and equipment storage room. The room is also where used cooking grease is taken before it is cleaned and put in the used cooking oil reservoir in the back. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulation of dust, dirt, grease, food residue, and other debris. Discussed with PIC and Staff about getting the floor cleaned, and additional measures to assist staff in keeping the floor clean, namely using temporary cardboard under the used cooking grease container. Ensure the floors are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed that the bathrooms that are used by women (womens room and employee bathroom) do not have covered trash cans. PIC was notified. Ensure that all bathrooms used by women have covered trash cans.
findings.citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed raw bacon being stored above cut onions in the prep cooler bottom area. CORRECTED: The PIC was informed and moved the bacon below and the onions above. Ensure that food is protected from cross contamination by storing raw animal food below ready-to-eat foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed that disposable containers were stored upright without protection. CORRECTED: The PIC was notified, the top container was discarded and the remaining containers were inverted. Ensure that single-service and single-use articles are protected from debris through cover or inversion.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed there is an accumulation of food residue, grease, and other debris on the surface underneath the grills. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, grease, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the surface underneath the grills are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed a mop stored with the head in the mop bucket. The PIC was informed and they moved the mop onto the hanger during the inspection. Ensure that mops are always stored in a position that allows the head to air dry.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed there was an open jug of milk in the front clear double cooler that was not date marked. The PIC stated the jug had been opened several days ago. The milk was correctly date marked during the inspection. The inspector suggested the PIC add labeling open milk to the kitchen’s closing routine. Ensure that all ready-to-eat, temperature control for safety foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours are date marked to indicate the 7-day maximum (day 1 being the day food was opened).
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Observed the container of sugar in the dry storage room had a bowl being used as a scoop. The PIC was educated that scoops for ready-to-eat foods must have a handle to avoid contact with food. The PIC discarded the bowls during the inspection. Ensure that dispensing utensils for ready-to-eat foods are stored with their handles not in contact with food to avoid contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed the rinsing surface to the left of the dish machine is not properly sealed to the wall in some locations. There is a gap between the caulking attached to the wall and the rinsing table surface. The surface must be re-sealed (ex. caulked) to the wall to make it smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure that the rinsing table surface is sealed to the wall by the next routine inspection.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Observed that no one at the facility has a valid allergen awareness certificate. One of the PIC’s (Jason) stated he will be re-taking the test. Ensure that someone at the facility has completed the allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Observed the PIC could not locate employee health reporting forms. The PIC was provided with copies during the inspection and employees present at the facility signed the forms. Remaining employees will sign the forms when they report to work. Ensure that all employees sign health reporting forms stating they will report information about their health to the PIC and the signed forms remain at the facility.

2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed the handwashing sink at the front bar was not being used. The PIC stated that employees working in the front bar wash their hands in the kitchen. The PIC was instructed that this hand washing sink must be used by employees working in the front bar. The hand sink was supplied with paper towels, hand soap, and a hand washing sign during the inspection. The PIC was also instructed to educate employees about only washing hands at this hand sink when working at the front bar.

5-203.11: (A) Specified under LAW, facility must have a number of HANDWASHING SINKS necessary for their convenient use by EMPLOYEESS. (B) If APPROVED, automatic handwashing may be substituted. (C) IF APPROVED, chemically treated towelettes can be used.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the following food contact surfaces needed to be cleaned due to an accumulation of soil: (1) Blade of the can opener; and (2) Ice machine baffles. The PIC cleaned the ice baffles during the inspection. The can opener was removed and also cleaned during the inspection. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are cleaned to sight and touch.


4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Observed there was not a sanitizer bucket made when inspectors arrived. The facility was in operation cooking and serving customers. A employee made a sanitizer bucket during the inspection. Ensure there is always a sanitizer bucket available during all hours of operation. 

4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the bucket holding the ice scoop had an accumulation of soil on the bottom. The PIC removed the bucket and scoop and set them by the triple sink for cleaning. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
Observed there is a leak underneath the triple sink. The PIC was aware of the issue and a plumber had already been called to schedule service. The inspector will return on 08/07/2024 to check if the leak has been fixed. Ensure plumbing systems are maintained in good repair.

5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed a mop being stored with the head in the water of a mop bucket and a mop with the head in the mop sink. The PIC moved the mops into a position where the head can air dry during the inspection. Ensure that mops are always stored in a position that allows the head to air dry when not in use.

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following physical facilities need to be cleaned: (1) Left of the ice machine; (2) Between the backs of cooking equipment; and (3) Under the front bar. Ensure that physical facility are cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed several dishes throughout the facility which were visibly contaminated with mouse droppings. All food-contact surfaces in the facility must be cleaned thoroughly to prevent further contamination. Additionally, inspector observed several dishes which have not been cleaned properly and had stuck on food remaining. All food-contact surfaces must be cleaned and sanitized. SCDPH supervisor will return today to ensure that all food-contact surfaces are free of contaminants. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Mouse droppings and food residue/debris are observed primarily in the small dry storage area off the rear of the ware washing area. These mouse droppings were observed on surfaces including but not limited to pan lids, plastic containers, drinking glasses, equipment, boxes including a box of mustard containers, among others. Pest control has been out three times to treat the facility. Glue traps and bait traps are located throughout the facility. Some presumably old mouse droppings are observed in containers in the back dry storage area, a container of single-use plastic utensils, and in wall corners which have not been properly cleaned. Dirty dishes throughout the facility provide harborage conditions for rodent infestations. SCDPH supervisor will return this evening to ensure that the facility is clean and mice have ben appropriately managed. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed several areas of the wall which are not coved/sealed which have facilitated the entry of rodents into the facility. Additionally, several ceiling tile of the drop ceiling remain missing. All areas which open to the interior sides of walls must be sealed to prevent entry and proliferation of mice. All ceiling tile must be replaced. Ensure that all areas of the facility are sealed to prevent the entry of pests. A follow-up is issued for 12/11/2023 to ensure that maintenance has been completed satisfactorily. 

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
The facility has been cited for multiple priority/priority foundation violations resulting in near closure of the establishment due to their severity. Additionally, the facility has repeat violations from the previous inspection which was the pre-opening of the facility. The combination of these factors and the obvious foodborne illness risk factors observed during the inspection indicate that active managerial control of the facility is not present. The person-in-charge of the establishment is required to ensure that compliance is maintained during operations. A follow-up is issued for 30-days to ensure that active managerial control of the facility has been established and is effective in ensuring compliance with Food Code requirements as adopted. Inspector will return on 11/30/2023. 

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

The PERSON IN CHARGE shall: (A) FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations not conducted in private home/room with sleeping quarters;  (B) restricted access ; (C) visitors comply with Code; (D) monitor EMPLOYEES' handwashing; (E) monitor deliveries;  (F) approved source/unadulterated;  (G) proper cooking TCS Food; (H) proper cooling ; (I) monitoring temperatures; (J) consumer advisory conveyed; (K) proper sanitizing;  (L) buffets are controlled;  (M) preventing cross-contamination of RTE FOOD with bare hands; (N) EMPLOYEES are properly trained in FOOD; (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of responsibility to report information about health; (P) Written procedures and plans are maintained and implemented as required. Pf

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed x2 employees using improper procedure to wash hands including failure to use a barrier to turn off the faucet and the proper duration. Manager discussed proper procedure with all staff members present during the inspection. Corrected on site and no further follow-up required for this violation. Ensure that ALL staff are aware of proper hand washing procedure and frequency.

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
The hand washing sink in the mens bathroom was not stocked with paper towels and the dryer was not functioning during the inspection. Ensure that all hand sinks are stocked with paper towels or drying device at all times. A 10-day follow-up is being issued to ensure that all hand sinks are properly stocked with soap and paper towels (or dryer in the bathroom). Inspector will return on November 9, 2023.

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Several dry food items located in the dry storage area were observed to be contaminated with mouse feces. All foods must be protected from any source of contamination to ensure that they are safe for public service. Foods which are contaminated have beend discarded by staff at the facility. A follow-up is issued for November 2, 2023 to ensure that foods are properly protected and are not contaminated with additonal feces at that time. 

3-101.11: FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Several food contact surfaces including containers holding food and metal pans are observed to be significantly soiled with mouse feces. Food-contact surfaces must be cleaned and sanitized ANY time that contamination occurs. Ensure that all food-contact surfaces are cleaned and sanitized and that no mouse droppings are present on any items which may contact food. A follow-up is issued for November 2, 2023 to evaluate compliance. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
During the inspection, inspector observed mouse droppings throughout the facility. The droppings had a lustrous appearance indicating that they are fresh and were accompanied by evident mouse footprints present in the foods in the dry storage area. Mouse droppings were observed in plastic containers of dry foods, on boxes of dry foods, on an open plate with a dry food in the employee food storage area, on pans and other cookware, in the corners of the walls/floors in the kitchen and dry storage areas, on countertops, and diffusely through the junk storage area. The smell of urine was observed by both inspector and SCDPH supervisor in the dry storage and junk storage areas. Due to the ubiquitous presence of mouse droppings throughout the facility, SCDPH EH director AA was contacted to visit the facility to establish next steps. AA discussed with PIC the conditions at the facitlity, preventive measure and corrective actions. AA advised PIC that the facility may remain open but must deep clean all areas with mouse droppings and adjust the frequency of cleaning and pest control to eliminate the rodent problem within the facility. Inspector observed several holes/gaps in the front and rear doors to the facility that are sufficiently large to allow entry of pests into the facility. The facility must seal these holes to prevent entry from these exterior areas. Foods must be sealed properly in plastic containers to prevent further infestation. Facility was advised that if corrective actions are not sufficient SCDPH will seek closure to ensure the safety of the public. A follow-up is issued for Thursday November 2, 2023.

6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Residue and debris has begun to accumulate on the nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment within the facility. Equipment must be cleaned often enough to prevent the accumulation of residue and/or debris on any of its surfaces. Ensure that cleaning of hard to reach areas of equipment are checked and cleaned often enough to remain clean.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION(S) (PO).

Food code requires that the facility maintain indoor materials in such a condition as to make all surfaces exposed to food and/or water SMOOTH, NON-ABSORBENT AND EASILY CLEANABLE. During the pre-opening of the facility PIC was advised to close/replace missing ceiling tile and caulk all counters without sufficient space to permit cleaning behind the equipment. Neither caulking nor ceiling tile replacement has been completed as of the inspection today. Additionally, inspector observed that the base coving underneath the triple sink along the East wall of the kitchen is peeling from the wall allowing the entry of food and water into the wall. Lastly, there is a piece of wall covering in the warewashing area which has peeled away from the wall as well. Ensure that all areas subject to food/moisture are smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.
